pr_title: RemoveDirectoryRecursive: fix delete of mount points
pr_body:
Fixes #86249.

Junctions have the same `WIN32_FIND_DATA` characteristics as volume mount points, but are deleted differently. Previous code did not differentiate between the two and tried to use `DeleteVolumeMountPoint` on both. This resulted in `ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER` (when executed by an elevated process) when `mountPoint` was a junction. Since `RemoveDirectory` will remove junctions also, the fix is to only call `DeleteVolumeMountPoint` for actual volume mount points.

issue_context.title: Directory.Delete(path, recursive: true) fails on directories containing junctions
issue_context.body:
### Description

On Windows, when recursively deleting a directory containing a junction, [`System.IO.Directory.Delete(String, Boolean)`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.io.directory.delete?view=net-7.0#system-io-directory-delete(system-string-system-boolean)) fails.

Symbolic links work as expected.

### Reproduction Steps

Since there's no API to create junctions, this is mostly easily reproduced in powershell:

```
New-Item -Type Directory 'parent'
New-Item -Type Directory 'target'
New-Item -Type Junction 'parent/link' -Target (Resolve-Path 'target')

try {
    [System.IO.Directory]::Delete((Resolve-Path "parent"), $true)
}
catch {
    $_.Exception.ToString() | Write-Host
}
```

### Expected behavior

The parent directory and junction should be removed successfully.

### Actual behavior

The junction is removed, but the parent directory is left behind. The exception message depends on whether the script is run as administrator or not:

<details>
  <summary>Non-admin</summary>

```
System.Management.Automation.MethodInvocationException: Exception calling "Delete" with "2" argument(s): "Access to the path 'link' is denied."
 ---> System.UnauthorizedAccessException: Access to the path 'link' is denied.
   at System.IO.FileSystem.RemoveDirectoryRecursive(String fullPath, WIN32_FIND_DATA& findData, Boolean topLevel)
   at System.IO.FileSystem.RemoveDirectory(String fullPath, Boolean recursive)
   at CallSite.Target(Closure , CallSite , Type , Object , Boolean )
   --- End of inner exception stack trace ---
   at System.Management.Automation.ExceptionHandlingOps.CheckActionPreference(FunctionContext funcContext, Exception exception)     
   at System.Management.Automation.Interpreter.ActionCallInstruction`2.Run(InterpretedFrame frame)
   at System.Management.Automation.Interpreter.EnterTryCatchFinallyInstruction.Run(InterpretedFrame frame)
   at System.Management.Automation.Interpreter.EnterTryCatchFinallyInstruction.Run(InterpretedFrame frame)
```
</details>

<details>
  <summary>Admin</summary>

```
System.Management.Automation.MethodInvocationException: Exception calling "Delete" with "2" argument(s): "The parameter is incorrect. : 'link'"
 ---> System.IO.IOException: The parameter is incorrect. : 'link'
   at System.IO.FileSystem.RemoveDirectoryRecursive(String fullPath, WIN32_FIND_DATA& findData, Boolean topLevel)
   at System.IO.FileSystem.RemoveDirectory(String fullPath, Boolean recursive)
   at CallSite.Target(Closure , CallSite , Type , Object , Boolean )
   --- End of inner exception stack trace ---
   at System.Management.Automation.ExceptionHandlingOps.CheckActionPreference(FunctionContext funcContext, Exception exception)
   at System.Management.Automation.Interpreter.ActionCallInstruction`2.Run(InterpretedFrame frame)
   at System.Management.Automation.Interpreter.EnterTryCatchFinallyInstruction.Run(InterpretedFrame frame)
   at System.Management.Automation.Interpreter.EnterTryCatchFinallyInstruction.Run(InterpretedFrame frame)
```
</details>

### Regression?

I'm able to reproduce this using the script in both powershell 5.1.19041.2673 (.NET Framework 4.8.4614.0), and powershell core 7.2.11 (.NET 6.0.16)

### Known Workarounds

Since the junction is removed, the operation can simply be retried to workaround the issue.

### Configuration

Reproduced on Windows 22H2 (build 19045.2846)

### Other information

_No response_

So, unfortunately not directly related to this issue here.

review_comments:
This won't be filtering juntions from volume mount points. Both will return without device path because GetImmediateLinkTarget always removes the `\??\` prefix. 

Which means that we will stop using `DeleteVolumeMountPoint` and will always be using `RemoveDirectory` for actual volume mount points. Surprisingly, your test doesn't fail due to this but we should avoid intrudicing the risk.
